summary: Upheld against a live population of two. One blocked record's blocker has evaporated -- the six interleaved-classic files it said were absent from build/listen are all staged now with a full auditionable set and an index row each, restaged this session -- so selection is skipping a task whose material is on disk. The other is still correctly blocked: it refuses a corpus search against a dirty tree, and the tree is dirty right now. I could not reproduce the verify's figure of three and report the one I measured instead. My own probe for the same defect over partial records returned 4 hits of which 3 were the regex matching the literal 'host' in a scratch grant -- the ninth wide-vs-real split today and the first I built myself. The valuable output is the unblocking, which needs a plan grant I do not hold, and which must carry the user's standing note that these six are RobTracker rather than Rob_Hubbard and stay low priority.

The retraction-collision case -- a grep for a retracted sentence hits the retraction that is required to quote it -- is now in CLAUDE.md beside the sibling's rule, added incrementally rather than rewritten.

Upheld, and narrowed to exactly one task. The historical instance checks out -- the v0.5.459 artefact record read done across up to two commits that could have changed emission (three touched python/h2g, but one was the regeneration and one declares no behaviour change) -- and the 665939c replacement correctly declares itself recurring and unclosable. But that declaration is prose in a field nothing reads: the plan schema has no recurrence field and closure is `outcome == done` alone, so the obligation is protected only by nobody having filed a done record for it. A cue-word audit of the 101 open verifies returns 18 hits of which 17 are one pasted grading clause -- the third pasted sentence measured this session to be ~94% of a wide count -- which is itself the argument for keying the fix on a declared field rather than on prose. Opened an in-repo plan_audit check_j with its grant, and filed the schema half as plugin work per the standing decision.
The counter-container rule is in CLAUDE.md with its four measured instances archived in docs/LESSONS.md, pinned by a new test the agent sabotaged and proved fails.

The comparability rule now sits beside KNOWN_BAD where the next candidate is chosen, naming all three outcomes with grep anchors to the scattered evidence -- and every figure is labelled historical, because the calibration artefact is still stamped v0.5.474 at 60 s.
An id prefix is a naming convention rather than a type: ^ab-N matches 6 closed ids where only 3 are real AB grants, now recorded as a rule in CLAUDE.md with the instance archived and graded.

The plan holds one task that cannot satisfy its own verify, not eight: Powerplay, whose decision tells it to write presets.json it held r: only -- now widened and re-verified, with the first 62-of-74 detector thrown away as self-measuring.

The window guard's skip is right and its invisibility is now gone: a new sibling test fails once, naming both windows and every figure that went quiet, while the assertions themselves still skip rather than compare two different quantities. The roster of window-guarded figures is DERIVED from the module's own source rather than hand-listed, so it cannot go stale at the moment a new guarded figure is added, and a vacuity assertion fires if that set is ever empty. Sabotage-verified twice: moving FIGURE_WINDOW without re-measuring now yields 1 failed / 6 passed / 3 skipped where it used to yield a green 7 passed / 3 skipped, and hollowing out the guarded set fails the guard rather than satisfying it. 10 passed, 0 failed, reverted and proved reverted.

The plan had exactly one prose-only prerequisite -- ab-9's GATE on the regrid id, which now has a real depends_on edge -- against 22 false positives from one pasted priority sentence, and the gate turned out to be satisfied already.

No open verify promises to create something that already exists -- the one narrow hit is this task quoting the defect and the two wide hits are 'which this task only READS' matched across an unrelated clause, so the family is settled with nothing written.

Regenerated at -t 180 (not the old 60, so the artefact matches the restaged listening set and FIDELITY.md): generator 0.5.471 -> 0.5.479, head df80762 -> 5a2fa2d, and calibrated false -> TRUE, which is the field the task is named for. No inherited span, and the verdicts are unchanged -- but the reason is now located rather than guessed: Action_Biker and 5_Title_Tunes have approved_sha == current_sha so they can never inherit, while ACE_II and Devils_Galop have shas that DIFFER and are the repo's only two inheritance candidates, coming back uncalibrated solely because the approved build is not on disk -- their .sng files exist but hold the current build, which a filename check cannot distinguish. `approvals.py --recover` is the one flag that would settle it and it writes build/listen, which this task does not grant, so I stopped and opened it. Tree fitness was proven before running: the only non-comment change under python/h2g since the artefact's label is the version string, and the byte-exact fixture passes.
The closure that broke is now a module-level pack_into and three tests cover it -- one calling the REAL pack_sid -- and sabotaging its mkdir reproduces the original FileNotFoundError exactly.

artefact_freshness.py now says which way it errs: STALE prints as a conservative upper bound naming the corpus byte-hash and tests/test_commando.py as the two things that can settle it, and NOT STALE prints as an exact guarantee needing no confirmation. The path-based rule is untouched -- a docstring-only edit still reports STALE, because that is the sound bound and not the defect -- and the only downgrade is an explicit caller-driven confirmed_unchanged, with no heuristic guessing docstring from code. check_freshness stays pure, re-verified by me with the docstring stripped via ast after that exact check produced a false alarm once before. 21 passed, 0 failed; two mutations, one of which SWAPS the two verdicts' certainty and fails five tests, so the suite pins which verdict is the uncertain one rather than merely that hedging exists.

Census taken by instrumenting the clamp itself and restoring patterns.py with the restore proven by sha before any figure was quoted: 34 of 89 corpus files clamp a note byte, 698 events, and the split that matters is 24 files clamping a byte PAST their own 96-entry table (557 events) against 9 clamping only real entries $5C-$5F that Goattracker cannot name (140 events), plus Action_Biker clamping the $FF marker. The bound came from FreqTable's own docstring rather than being invented. So Commando is not special -- it is 1 of 24, behind Ricochet at 71 clamps and beside Last_V8's eighteen distinct past-the-table bytes -- and the fixture-recut decision is about a class rather than a file. $68 recurs across seven unrelated files and is recorded as a LEAD, since only Commando's has been traced. Recorded beside the clamp, comment-only (the non-comment diff is empty); 23 passed with one test pinning the arithmetic the split rests on and two mutations each failing by name.

No uniform clock ratio hides in either low-melody row: Commodore_64_Music_Examples paces at a perfect 1.000 once paired correctly and Dragons_Lair_Part_II's is a loose 0.937 behind a subtune remap, so both stay harness artefacts on stronger evidence.
Retracted a false claim in docs/LESSONS.md: all eight probed fidelity-json keys exist under aliases rather than being absent, re-verified against the artefact.

The forever-loop passage in docs/LESSONS.md is now graded HISTORY at v0.5.375 with the current v0.5.476 reading beside it (+0.14 s, 291 attacks against 291); one cited source path was fabricated and is corrected here.

The title's claim is refuted by the code -- voices_end_together has existed since v0.5.433 and is tested -- and the real defect was legalise_restarts' docstring asserting its own absence four lines above the call, now retracted with the Confuzion rows-versus-writes distinction recorded beside it.

The mutation is now visible: reverting convert_at's `return Converted(...)` to the old bare packed path fails exactly one named test, where at c2cb76a it left the suite at 0 failed because every test injected a fake. The agent found no analogue of pack_into's early-failure point -- convert_at's own .sng write IS a subprocess call -- and said so rather than adding a third fake, faking only subprocess.run and pack_sid so the real function's real control flow reaches the real Converted construction. I re-ran the scoped suite (41 passed) and read the call site rather than trusting the summary, and found and fixed the file's header docstring still claiming nothing there calls convert_at -- 9ec29bf's defect, in the file being strengthened.

Whole-corpus ablation (89 files x 2 arms, -t 180), arm A validated against build/fidelity.json on 89/89 output_shas and adsr values. cut_release reaches only 31 of 89 files (58 byte-identical); it is gated on det.envelope_cut plus a per-record EFFECT_PER_FRAME check. On those 31 it costs adsr on 30 and helps it on ZERO, while helping rel (release_tail_agreement) on 29 and hurting it on zero -- release_tail_ours_longer goes to 0 on all 31. So the verify's expected split is not two disjoint file populations but one population and two opposed columns: the option zeroes the release nibble in the instrument record, which adsr charges for every sounding frame of the note in order to buy the release tail that rel scores. The second sub-mechanism (original at $0000, we hold the record) is bit-identical on both arms of all 31 files and is the entire remaining ceiling on Geoff Capes. Three of the lowest-adsr files are inert under the ablation, so their deficit has a different cause. Nothing was adopted, removed or committed; seven follow-ups proposed.

The rule is in CLAUDE.md beside its two siblings with the instance archived in docs/LESSONS.md -- and the agent corrected my miscount, since grep -c counts lines while the same file reads 3, 5 or 0 depending on the method.

Measured hold, nrun and noise per instrument on four files at -t 180 and HEAD 5a2fa2d, validating the calling convention by independently reproducing all four output_sha. The three columns do NOT move together: across 12 nrun instruments, hold's -1 reaches nrun on exactly 2, and the noise frame count is never a per-run -1 on any file. The discriminator is exact on 12/12 -- nrun sees hold's -1 only when the original's modal noise run equals its modal held note length (the noise IS the note); where the original's noise is a 1-2 frame attack tick, nrun is structurally blind (8 matches) and where it is neither, nrun misses by -5 or +14 rather than -1. Zoolook's 1.000 nrun beside a 199-frame noise loss is that blindness, not agreement. Geoff Capes, the single-file coincidence that opened this, already split internally: both its nrun instruments read hold delta -1 and only one shows a noise-run -1, and its -24 noise delta is an 84-frame run we never sound offset by 60 frames we add. A multiplier explanation for Zoolook's mixed census was raised and refuted against the corpus artefact. No emitter touched, no bound claimed.

Kings of the Beach (ingame) is diagnosed, not finished: its aud 0.66 is a missing pulse-width sweep (pul 3/1026, pspan 0.00x) that detection does read, with coverage, length and every sequence column already clean.

Refuted. The four flags are byte-inert on many files -- 216 (file, flag) pairs measured in-process at HEAD, slides 61 / vibrato_command 64 / cut_release 58 / rest_keyoff 33, with 0 ablation aborts -- but ZERO of those 216 is set in a per-song entry: all come from the `always` block, which has no song entries for any of the four. `prune_inert` operates on `chosen`, the per-song SELECTED flags, so it never sees them and is not failing; the set of pairs it should have removed is empty. Removing them would be a defect rather than a cleanup, because the same four flags are LIVE on 140 pairs. presets.json was not regenerated -- there is nothing to prune, and the artefact guard refuses presets.py from this dirty tree, which I did not override. The refutation belongs beside prune_inert in python/presets.py, which this task grants read-only, so I stopped and opened it with the right grant rather than widening my own.

Settled by the recording arm: nothing to fix, because the trade is real. fidelity.py now states, immediately before the `gate` entry and introducing the pair, that gate and hold are ONE FRAME COUNTED TWICE -- moving one moves the other the other way and no setting satisfies both -- with the three measured arms from 4b5d7f0 (2 calls buys gate 72% and pays fetch 4 of 4; 1 call pays gate 15 points and buys nothing; 0 calls buys fetch 0 of 4 and pays five columns) and the consequence that raising either is a choice, never an improvement. Both entries already carried half of this at HEAD, which I verified against `git show` rather than assuming. The first sabotage run caught ME: two of my three tests passed over their own subject's deletion, one matching an unrelated '1 call' elsewhere in the file and one matching the surviving words 'gate bit' -- this repo's container-vs-subject failure, in tests written to prevent decay, and the second time today my own tests missed their own mutation. Fixed structurally by slicing the block out of the source and asserting against the slice; all three mutations now fail exactly one correct test each. 199 passed, 0 failed.

Action Biker measured and fully attributed: gate is above the corpus median so it owes nothing, the 62 drum runs are each exactly one frame short (682/744 = 11/12), and adsr 69% decomposes without remainder into a zeroed release nibble and an unreproduced note-end envelope kill.

Confuzion measured at HEAD c2cb76a (h2g 0.5.478), conversion sha 7cbac3906726 validated against the harness and the corpus row before anything was concluded. Coverage needs -t 310 (cov 1.000; -t 180 gives 0.590). All 26 columns reported with both attack counts (1022/1022, retrig 1.00 -- nothing rose by removing events). Against the 89 measured seconds=180 corpus rows, eight columns are below median and the literal and robust log-space readings agree on every one: adsr 0.2097 (med 0.8044), vib 0.7308 (0.9830), depth 1.3549 (0.8166), hold 0.0000 (0.1056), pul 1.7962x (0.9481), pphase 0.5385x (0.8750), aud 0.8513 (0.9000), loud 0.8965 (0.9503). Pace is exact -- median 1.000, IQR 1.000-1.000 over 1019 gaps, drift 0.0 frames across 8988, and the least-squares fit agrees at 1.000, so there is no fit/median divergence. --diagnose is clean, so no harness defect stands in the way. Six columns are attributed with figures: adsr to the release nibble zeroed by cut_release (A/D/S identical in all six dominant mismatch pairs); hold to 8-of-8 `fetch` at delta -1, tied to gate's 1022 surplus frames = exactly our attack count; pul to voice 0's step halving 64->32 at identical span (pspan 1.0039); pphase to voice 0 opening on 3 widths of 9 while visiting 52 against 28; vib to the per-note Goattracker vibrato command, by ablation -- removing it recovers 148 reversals (0.7308 -> 0.9624) while removing the instrument-record vibrato makes it far worse (0.042), which is the direction that proves which mechanism is the defect. depth and aud/loud are declared UNATTRIBUTED. Two refutations worth carrying forward: the vib x depth = 0.9902 compensating pair is a coincidence, not a mechanism -- depth is flat at 1.3487 while vib moves to 0.9624, so the product goes to 1.2981; and gate here is ABOVE median at 0.7656 with 1020 of 1020 releases matched, so the Zoolook mechanism is absent and the set is now seven above, one below. The `slides` option is byte-inert on this file too -- the fourth in a row. No bound declared, no option adopted, no file outside the scratch dir written.

Food_Feud at -t 180 is below the corpus median on melody/seq/pitch (attributed: one contiguous voice-0 passage, 72 of 748 attacks, played exactly -12 semitones because the version-0 track reader emits no orderlist transpose), on slides/depth (one vibrato mechanism, 1.84x the frames at 0.56x the depth), and on filt/cut (filter overshoot, both zeroed by ablating `filters`), with pphase and wave below and unattributed, gate ABOVE the median for the fifth song running, and --pace showing a median 1.000 and zero drift so timing is not a defect.

At -t 180 with the shipped presets Geoff Capes covers its whole original (cov 100%, no widening needed) and is below the 89-row corpus medians on adsr (0.1211 vs 0.8044), nrun (0.50 vs 1.00), hold (0.00 vs 0.1056), vib and depth in log space, and marginally on noise, retrig and len -- adsr is attributed by ablation to `--cut-release` (0.1211 -> 0.8147), hold/nrun/noise to one `fetch` -1, vib/depth to one vibrato-rate mechanism (0.7425 x 1.3524 = 1.0042), retrig and len left unattributed, with the pace median 1.000 (IQR 1.000-1.000, fit 0.949 diverging) and zero drift ruling out the clock.

Kings of the Beach fully attributed: the only real defect is a duty cycle frozen at 3.1% because the traced subtune's single instrument has a set-only pulse program, while wave and hold turn out to be a silent-park tail and a one-instrument slot artefact rather than defects.

Knucklebusters measured at -t 196, the minimum full-coverage window, and the window itself changes the verdict: loud reads above median there and below at -t 200, because our conversion ends 4.16 s early and a wider window charges it for the gap.

Measured Saboteur_II.sid at 665939c/v0.5.476 against corpus medians derived from the 89 measured, seconds=180 rows of build/fidelity.json. window_coverage 1.0 needs -t 260 (the original ends at 249.18 s); -t 180 reads 0.7224, and both windows are reported with every column and both attack counts (2566/2564 and 3622/3622). --diagnose is clean: identity subtune correspondence, all three voices ratio 1.00 and pitches 100%. --pace medians 1.000 (IQR 0.909-1.100 over 2963 gaps) with drift +0.00 frames/1000 across 12458 frames; the least-squares fit 0.999 agrees with the median, so there is no divergence to read, and --pace declines the file on its own 30% matched-note threshold. Below the corpus median under both log-space readings: bend 0.71x, depth 0.52x, pphase 0.67x, filt 1.70x, cut 1.50x, wave 87%, loud 93%. Attributed by ablation: filt, cut and ~64% of loud to the `filters` emitter's routing duty -- we hold the filter in circuit 11520 of 12550 frames where the player routes it in on 6400, and sweep a band 1.66x too wide; bend, depth and the slides surplus to one mechanism, the `vibrato` emitter's step size (right rate, right prevalence, half the swing); wave to a one-frame-late waveform on voices 1 and 2 (not wave_program, which is carrying the column, and not the gate, which accounts for 12% of the deficit); pphase to voice 0's note-opening duty width, which survives pulse=False. len and loud's 0.0751 residual are stated as unattributed. Three refutations recorded: gate reads ABOVE the median for the sixth file running; the staged 'no legato' note's 8046-vs-1631 does not reproduce (10667 vs 9682, the deficit 933 ties confined to voice 0); and the preset's `slides` and `vibrato_command` flags are both byte-inert here. No bound declared, no preset adopted, no converter file touched -- six follow-up ids proposed instead.

Samantha Fox measured and attributed: gate turns out to be ABOVE the corpus median so the brief was wrong again, and adsr 0.48 decomposes without remainder into an unreproduced note-end envelope kill, a zeroed release nibble and one envelope record we never emit.

Sanxion measured at -t 340 for full coverage, and the window mattered: gate was 30% artefact, pspan inverts, and two unnamed columns are worse than the named one -- with the wave deficit attributed to one firstwave frame per attack plus a fragmented drum.

Sigma Seven measured and attributed, refuting its own brief: it is below median on four fraction columns rather than one, and every note's frequency lands one frame after its gate-on -- a defect on 100% of notes that costs a single point of pitch and nothing else.

Supersedes the earlier measure-zoolook record to correct one figure: the hold census is 1 match / 3 fetch / 5 slot, not 3/2/4, verified against the artefact and by an independent re-run -- every other figure in that record, including gate 0.3758 below the 0.6270 median and its hard-restart attribution, stands unchanged.

Both frame-axis outcomes now sit together in the naming_split docstring, labelled HISTORICAL at 7bcd3fe with HEAD's distance and what to re-run -- and the same figure in a printed report string was past-tensed and labelled too.

Settled, and neither reading was wrong -- they count different events. python/listen.py:939 traces OUR side with run_siddump's default calls=1 while listen.py:885-887 packs at -S3, so the packed tune plays at 1/3 speed for the whole staging trace. The 5.937 factor decomposes exactly into 4.529 (multiplier) x 1.311 (window), and the multiplier half is 4.53 rather than 3.0 because the missing -m makes the trace both slow AND a prefix -- Saboteur_II's voice 1 ties 16 times in the first 60 s against 1903 over 180 s. At one window with both sides correct: Saboteur_II 0.918x, so it has NO legato defect and its staged note is a FALSE POSITIVE; Food_Feud 0.354x, a real defect concentrated in the third voice at 36/1396. 17 of the 23 staged 'No legato' notes are on -S>1 files and are all unreliable -- this is the listening set restaged this session. The repo already fixed this bug in fidelity.py at v0.5.96 and listen.py reintroduced it, licensed by a comment that states a true fact about gt2reloc's -S and draws a false conclusion about siddump's -m. DECISION: a tie dimension belongs, as a COUNT ratio not a share -- its own falsification showed the share is sampling-fragile (0.263 vs 0.127 on identical music). Nothing added, per the verify.

The discriminator held and became a rule: over all 32 corpus files whose noise_run_agreement is below 1.0 -- 141 nrun instruments, 138 pairing to a hold key -- 28 of 28 instruments whose original modal noise run equals its original modal held length propagate hold's -1 into nrun as an exact -1, and 0 of 76 others do. It rested on 2 positives this morning. 66 of the 76 negatives are floor-blind at a modal run of 1-3 frames, where a one-frame loss deletes the run rather than shortening it, and the remaining 10 miss by -105 to +299 and are documented as the same modal blindness rather than folded in as explained. Zoolook's 199 lost noise frames under a 100% nrun reading reproduce exactly. Both findings are now in the Dimension's printed text and pinned by three synthetic-fixture tests; two mutations in two different layers each fail their own test. 191 passed, 0 failed, build/fidelity.json untouched.

The gate is ours and it is one byte: FIRSTWAVE_TESTBIT = 0x09 at goatwriter.py:360, emitted as byte +8 of every instrument record at 3263-3268 -- both lines read from disk by me. Traced frames show it on the LAST frame of every note's slot (Rasputin $0A09 ours `40 09 |81 81 80 x9 09| 41 41` against the original's `40 40 |81 81 80 x10| 41 41`), and being below $10 it fails both the noise walk and the held-note walk on the same frame -- which is why our run and hold distributions are identical MULTISETS, not merely equal modes. The wavetables rule out a wavetable restart: every instrument measured ends its program on noise, and the one whose program does select a later non-noise waveform is exactly the one where run 2 != hold 11. Causality settled by A/B: forcing no_test_restart collapses 486 Confuzion runs into one 8993-frame run against the original's 8998. But the apparent catastrophe is MEASUREMENT -- noise_runs is gate-blind and the original's '8998-frame run' is a latched waveform on a gated-off voice; reduced as (noise AND gate) both sides read 486 runs of modal 21, 7542 vs 7537 frames, five frames apart rather than 491. Emitter untouched.

Answered both halves. A Goattracker INSTRUMENT structurally cannot carry a phase -- one pulse pointer, reloaded at every note -- but a PATTERN ROW can, via command $09 CMD_SETPULSEPTR (patterns.py:143, read from disk) naming a per-(width,direction) entry point, and that mechanism is already implemented behind --pulse-phase and merely switched off. Forced on, Confuzion goes pphase 0.538 -> 0.923 with every other scalar column identical, still packing, and I confirmed four corpus files already carry the option, so adoption is routine rather than novel. Every historical pphase figure reproduced exactly, and the `pulse` ablation was re-run on all three files rather than cited -- it reaches each one (shas move, pul collapses) and leaves pphase bit-identical, so Food Feud is now ruled out too. The 'visits 52 vs 28' figure is corrected as MIS-FRAMED rather than stale: at the column's own bucket the visited sets are equal (13/13), and the 51/27 shape exists only at raw 12-bit resolution. Saboteur_II and Food_Feud are declined by the ENGINE gate, not the multiplier gate -- they run a pulse engine with no phase simulator, making the flag byte-inert, which is the correct 'sweep ruled out, mechanism unattributed' verdict for those two.

The --pace contradiction is settled against CLAUDE.md: the tool derives every printed figure from the median, the square-weighted fit reads 0.360 on Tarzan where the drift is zero, and the wrong instruction has been removed from CLAUDE.md, the archive and all twelve queued measure tasks.

plan_audit gains check_g, which classifies rather than counts -- 17 naive vocabulary hits over the population it considers, 0 after four structural exemptions including one the verify never named -- with its suite now committed beside the module and re-sabotaged from there.

check_h and check_i added as module-level classifiers beside check_g, both silent on the live plan and both proved live by four named mutations -- disabling either exemption resurfaces exactly the wide matches it suppresses, and dropping either half of check_i's guard brings back either ab-9 or the ILV false positives. The agent re-derived rather than reproduced: check_h's 3-wide/0-real matches history exactly, check_i's wide count is 68 rather than the historical 23 and it said so instead of forcing a match, since a wide count belongs to the probe and only the classified count belongs to the plan. I re-ran both (19 passed; no H or I section on the live plan while A/C/F still fire) and fixed the file's header, which still described only check_g and claimed to live in scratch -- the third stale-prose find of this cycle.

_preset_opts now warns instead of silently returning the always block for a name absent from a populated songs list -- warn rather than raise because listen.py's --diff path legitimately takes that route, and the 32 warnings it raises are exactly the 6 corpus files with no entry.
The pulse split-leg census covers all 24 triangle-pulse files against the 255-row budget and names the overflow: Crazy_Comets needs 319 rows and fails at instrument 17.

All eleven are one mechanism -- `_pulse_layout`'s `silent` branch, pointer 0, the pulse table full when the record was written -- and the SET is {Knucklebusters 27/28/29, Mr_Meaner 15/16/17, Rock_Tells_the_Tale 13/14/15/16/17}, corroborated by the emitter's own log lines summing 3+3+5. The off-by-one was actively excluded by wrapping _pulse_layout to read `lead`. The third cause is real and is about consequence: allocation is POSITIONAL, so the losers are always the tail of the record list -- six of the eleven are never named in any pattern while Rock GT16, named 176 times with a pulse-only wavetable, gets nothing. Scarcity is confined: exactly four of 89 files reach PTBL >= 240 of 255, and Gerry_the_Germ at 246 with pulse_phase already on has the least headroom of any file that has not yet lost an instrument -- and is precisely the one the instrumentation cannot see, which it flagged rather than skipped. Sharing identical programs would fit all of Knucklebusters (23 distinct costing 249 against a 253 budget, versus 261 wanted) and neither of the other two. Validated by reproducing 89 of 89 stored output_sha with the _preset_opts warning promoted to an error -- the strongest calling-convention defence of the session.

The version-pinned artefact regeneration is replaced by a version-less recurring obligation whose done-condition is test_output_sha reading 0 disagreeing, and which says in its own verify that it cannot be closed.

All 89 staged tunes now render at one 180 s window with 0 stale and a listening note each -- the set that needed staging was 34 rather than the title's 23, and the new merge kept the 55 notes an overwrite would have destroyed.
All 89 staged tunes are now the conversion their measurement describes -- 0 stale, verified by sha -- but the set is 66 at 180 s and 23 at 120 s, so the uniform-window half is unmet and named.

All 4 decided tasks and all 7 decision records check out -- the 2 mode-flipped ones describe the work and the 2 interview-worded ones are still genuinely awaiting a human -- and a widened scan over all 106 tasks found 16 matches with 0 real defects behind them.

convert_at now returns Converted(sng, sid) and approvals stops rebuilding the .sng path by hand, with the old wording retracted where a grep lands -- but sabotaging convert_at's own return is invisible to the suite, because every test injects a fake, and that gap is opened rather than hidden.
Corrected the stale 'exercised by hand' docstring in test_sound_calibrate.py to say render_doc is now pinned; verified by my own diff inspection and suite run, not the agent's thin record.
No per-function coverage census exists to fix, so the nesting of survey.py's _ptrs was written down at its definition site instead; suites green.

The gatetimer floor is now pinned by a test sweeping the whole parameter space, and three named mutations each kill it -- one of them revealing the row_calls guard protects against a negative value, not just zero.

Nothing deleted and nothing owed here: the 13 prose entries are really 8, since five carry an id behind a dot, a capital, a parenthesis or a dash that the first-colon rule cannot see -- and the tail is stable while the log grows, so it needs no guard.

python/artefact_freshness.py works and its 13 tests and three sabotages stand, but its first real use produced a false positive -- STALE for a docstring-only emitter edit the Commando fixture proves moved no byte -- so its answer is a conservative upper bound and should say so.

The generator's rule -- not its output -- now scans for the first of a colon, a dot, a parenthesis or a ' -- ' whose head is a well-formed slug, with SLUG made case-insensitive, and the file was regenerated by re-running it as its own header demands. 461 entries become 471 over the current 548-record log, with the ten recovered ids named as a set and the prose residue falling 19 -> 8, each of those 8 read in full and confirmed a real sentence rather than a mis-split id. One of the brief's five 'separators' was correctly re-diagnosed as a case-sensitivity bug instead, and the dot's known sharp edge on decimals was documented rather than special-cased.
The either/or-record template is used 35 times and 30 uses were already fine -- the defect was 5 missing grants, now homed, with 0 remaining and the parallel lane down one as the price.

depth's two refusals now print apart: `-` where no record in the original carries a vibrato byte (nothing to compare, nothing to fix) and `-!` where the population exists and no instrument key was shared (the comparison did not happen -- a candidate for work, and the same shape as Powerplay Hockey's dash, which was a real defect).
